To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ICD 10 and DSM IV criteria sets for HKD and ADHD, respectively, are equivalent in their predictive validity.

HKD, ADHD, C, ADHD HI (hyper active impulsive subtype), and ADHD IA (inattentive subtype) had approximately equivalent predictive utility even when comorbiddity was controlled, that HKD and ADHD IA differed from normal controls on a number of measures, and that the HKD group had the highest rates of symptoms, impairment, and inhibitory control deficits.

1) HKD and ADHD have similar predictive validity, 2) the predictive validity of both HKD and ADHD is reduced when the effects of comorbidity are controlled for, and 3) the predictive validity is reduced to a similar degree for both HKD and the three ADHD subtypes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validity and clinical utility of the DSM IV and ICD 10 diagnostic criteria for ADHD and HKD.
the predictive validity of HKD and ADHD, while controlling for the influence of comorbidity.
the validity of the DSM-IV and ICD 10 diagnoses of ADHD and HKD, respectively, and the extent to which these disorders are associated with other psychiatric and cognitive problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ICD 10 and DSM IV criteria for HKD and ADHD C, HI and IA have equivalent predictive validity.
the predictive validity of HKD and ADHD C, ADHD Hl and ADHD IA are essentially equivalent and that both HKD and ADHD have superior predictive validity than normal controls.
the ICD 10 diagnosis of HKD has no advantage over DSM IV ADHD in terms of predictive validity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HKD, ADHD HI and IA were not different in their predictive validity, but all were different from ADHD C, and that all were different from normal controls.
HKD is a useful diagnostic entity, but that ADHD C and ADHD IA are also clinically useful and valid diagnoses.
HKD and ADHD are essentially equivalent in terms of the range of variables examined in this study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HKD is not a more valid diagnostic category for ADHD than ADHD C.
the predictive validity of ADHD and HKD are similar.
the predictive validity of HKD is comparable to that of ADHD C, ADHD IA, ADHD HI and is not compromised by the presence of comorbidity.
